warmup.description: Open the thoracic spine and prep the rotator cuff with controlled, deliberate movement before any loaded pressing or pulling.
movements: Cat-cow with shoulder blade squeeze at top — 10 reps
Thread-the-needle thoracic rotation — 8 reps each side
Prone Y-T-W raises (bodyweight) — 6 reps each position
Resistance band face pull — 15 slow reps
Dead hang or active hang from bar — 20–30 seconds

main_exercises.name: Barbell or Smith Machine Bent-Over Row
main_exercises.load_guidance: Heavier than a dumbbell row allows — find a load where the last 2 reps of each set require deliberate bracing. This is the strength anchor of the session.
main_exercises.form_cue: Hinge to roughly 45 degrees, brace your core before every rep, and pull the bar into your lower sternum — not your belly button.

main_exercises.name: Push-Up Variation (elevated feet or weighted vest if available, or standard)
main_exercises.load_guidance: Choose the hardest variation where you can maintain a perfectly rigid plank position for all reps — this is a skill-strength exercise, not a burnout movement.
main_exercises.form_cue: Lower your chest to the floor, not your hips — think of the push-up as a moving plank and keep your glutes squeezed throughout.

main_exercises.name: Cable or Band Face Pull
main_exercises.load_guidance: Very light — this is a postural corrective movement done for quality. If you can't hold the end position for one count every rep, reduce the load.
main_exercises.form_cue: Pull the rope or band to your nose with external rotation at the top — thumbs should end up pointing behind you, not at the ceiling.

main_exercises.name: Dumbbell Pullover (flat bench)
main_exercises.load_guidance: A moderate load you can control through a full range of motion — the stretch at the bottom is the stimulus, so never rush the eccentric.
main_exercises.form_cue: Keep a slight bend in the elbows throughout and stop the arc when your arms are parallel to the floor — going further loads the shoulder joint rather than the lats.

main_exercises.name: Standing Dumbbell Arnold Press
main_exercises.load_guidance: Lighter than a standard overhead press — the rotation adds range and complexity, so reduce load by roughly 20% compared to what you'd press straight.
main_exercises.form_cue: Start with palms facing your shoulders at chin height and rotate outward as you press, finishing with palms forward at the top.

main_exercises.name: Tricep Dips (bench or parallel bars) or Overhead Tricep Extension
main_exercises.load_guidance: For dips, use your bodyweight or add a dumbbell in your lap if bodyweight feels easy by rep 8. For the extension, pick a load where rep 11 is genuinely the last clean rep.
main_exercises.form_cue: For dips, keep your torso upright and elbows tracking straight back — forward lean shifts work to the chest. For the extension, keep your elbows pointing at the ceiling and still.

cooldown.description: Release tension in the lats, triceps, and posterior shoulder — structures that accumulate tightness from rowing and pressing patterns.
movements: Lat stretch in doorframe or against a wall — 45 seconds each side
Overhead tricep stretch — 30 seconds each side
Supine cross-body shoulder stretch — 30 seconds each side
Neck side bend with gentle hand pressure — 20 seconds each side

phase_notes.menstrual: The bent-over row demands core bracing that may feel uncomfortable if cramping is present — substitute the chest-supported dumbbell row from variant 1 as needed, or rest entirely.
phase_notes.follicular: Estrogen-supported recovery makes this a good week to add a small load increment to the barbell row and push-up variation and note your new baseline.
phase_notes.ovulatory: Peak neuromuscular output means the push-up variation and Arnold press may feel unusually crisp — this is a reliable window to test a harder push-up progression.
phase_notes.early_luteal: Complete the session as written; progesterone-driven fatigue is minimal in early luteal and most users will hit all sets without modification.
phase_notes.late_luteal: The pullover and face pull are forgiving in late luteal because the loads are inherently light — lean on those movements if energy is low and treat the barbell row sets as the one place to push rather than four.
